items.title: agibot-world/AgiBotWorld2026
items.summary: AgiBot’s 2026 real-world embodied-intelligence release, described as the follow-up to AgiBot World. Use it to train policies on real scenes. The card preview does not list the robot or the episode count.

items.title: lerobot/FineART
items.summary: 40,543 teleoperated episodes (1,718 hours) on a Trossen ALOHA-style two-arm robot, with 533,913 human-written subtask labels across 151 tasks. Scale AI collected it with LeRobot. Use it to train a policy that follows step-by-step instructions.

items.title: nvidia/PhysicalAI-Robotics-GR00T-X-Embodiment-Sim
items.summary: Simulated trajectories NVIDIA used to post-train GR00T N1. About 9,000 two-arm demos cover Franka grippers, Franka hands, and a GR1 humanoid, on tasks such as threading, lifting a tray, assembly, cleanup, sorting cans, and making coffee. Use it with Isaac GR00T.

items.title: willi19/autodex-gallery
items.summary: Real dexterous grasping from the CoRL 2026 AutoDex project. The robot tries a grasp, checks whether it worked, and resets the object, building a reusable grasp library. Download the grasp labels, trajectories, and multi-view video, or browse the gallery.

items.title: genrobot2025/Gen-HumanEgo
items.summary: 1,800+ hours of real first-person human demonstrations from a six-camera DAS-Ego rig, with motion and spatial labels added by GenRobot’s model. Use it as human-video supervision for embodied learning.

items.title: XDOF/ABC-130k
items.summary: Two-arm teleoperation on YAM stations, stored as MCAP files with subtask labels kept separate. The card calls it the largest open teleoperation set. Train and deploy with the code linked from abc.bot.

items.title: IPEC-COMMUNITY/language_table_lerobot
items.summary: LeRobot copy of Language Table. A real xArm follows instructions such as “push the blue cube to the center.” 442,226 episodes at 10 Hz. Use it for language-conditioned tabletop pushing.

items.title: OpenMOSS-Team/OmniAction
items.summary: Training data for RoboOmni, accepted at ICLR 2026. It targets robot manipulation from a broad audio-visual context, for policies that act without a single explicit command.

items.title: cadene/droid_1.0.1
items.summary: LeRobot v2.1 copy of DROID. 95,600 in-the-wild episodes from Franka arms at 15 Hz, with everyday instructions such as putting a block in a bowl. Use it to pretrain or fine-tune a real-arm policy.

items.title: IPEC-COMMUNITY/droid_lerobot
items.summary: Another LeRobot copy of DROID: 92,233 Franka episodes and 31,308 language tasks. Same use as #9, in a slightly different package.

items.title: genrobot2025/10Kh-RealOmin-OpenData
items.summary: Human two-hand household video. The card claims 13,000+ hours, 5 million clips, 3,000 contributors, and 10,000 real homes, with reconstructed hand trajectories. Use it for large-scale human-manipulation pretraining.

items.title: nureasoning/nuReasoning
items.summary: Driving dataset. Each clip has cameras, LiDAR, the vehicle state, a map, and written reasoning about long-tail traffic. Use it to train or test a driver that must explain its decision.

items.title: leggedrobotics/grand_tour_dataset
items.summary: ETH Zurich’s Grand Tour. An ANYmal D quadruped carrying the Boxi sensor box walked 49+ indoor and outdoor places, including campuses, forests, the Alps, stations, and industrial sites. LiDAR, cameras, IMU, and joint sensing for localization and navigation.

items.title: behavior-1k/2025-challenge-demos
items.summary: 10,000 simulated episodes of a Galaxea R1 Pro humanoid doing 50 household tasks, such as turning on a radio or putting away decorations. The demo set for the 2025 BEHAVIOR challenge.

items.title: nvidia/PhysicalAI-Robotics-Open-H-Embodiment
items.summary: NVIDIA’s community collection for surgical robots and ultrasound. Paired video and joint motion from tabletop drills, clinical procedures, and healthcare simulations, in LeRobot format.

items.title: simple-world-lab/HiFi-UMI-2K
items.summary: 2,000 hours of robot-free two-hand demonstrations from a portable six-camera rig, across 480+ scenes, with millimeter-level hand pose. Use it to learn manipulation from people, then retarget that motion to a robot.

items.title: agibot-world/AgiBotWorld-Beta
items.summary: Real mobile two-arm data. The card says 1 million+ trajectories, 2,976 hours, 100 robots, 100+ scenes, and 200+ tasks such as tying, opening jars, peeling, and sweeping, using dexterous hands and tactile sensors.

items.title: sourlreapwr/RobotArena-Benchmark
items.summary: Reconstructed manipulation scenes and RGB sequences for testing vision-language-action policies in simulation. A real robot video is turned into a physics scene. This is an evaluation set.

items.title: cadene/droid
items.summary: An earlier LeRobot packaging of the same DROID Franka collection, with the same kind of everyday language instructions. Use it like #9 and #10.

items.title: chenhn02/MetaFold
items.summary: Point-cloud trajectories of folding many kinds of garments, for robot cloth folding. The license is CC BY-NC-ND.

items.title: UCLA-VAIL/UrbanVerse-Assets-Sim-ready
items.summary: USD conversions of UCLA’s UrbanVerse-100K city objects, ready for Isaac Sim 5 and Isaac Lab. These are 3D props for urban simulation.

items.title: nvidia/PhysicalAI-Robotics-Manipulation-Kitchen-Demos
items.summary: 600 hours and 55,000 trajectories across 316 kitchen tasks. A person teleoperated a Franka Panda on an Omron mobile base. LeRobot format, for mobile kitchen manipulation.

items.title: configinc/HABIT
items.summary: Robot demonstrations recorded while people are in the scene, so a policy can learn human-aware behavior. For human-robot interaction and vision-language-action training.

items.title: nvidia/video-to-data-robot-dexterity-task-library-and-dataset
items.summary: Human hand demonstrations retargeted onto two Sharpa dexterous hands, plus robot episodes that replay those motions. A sample pack for NVIDIA’s video-to-robot pipeline.

items.title: HuggingFaceVLA/community_dataset_v3
items.summary: 791 community LeRobot datasets from 235 people, covering 46 robot types, gathered for SmolVLA-style pretraining. A mixed pool for a generalist policy.

items.title: IPEC-COMMUNITY/kuka_lerobot
items.summary: LeRobot copy of the Google Kuka bin-picking set. 209,880 episodes of a Kuka iiwa whose only instruction is “pick anything.”

items.title: RoboVerseOrg/roboverse_data
items.summary: The data bundle for RoboVerse, a unified simulation platform and benchmark for general robot learning. Use it inside that benchmark.

items.title: IPEC-COMMUNITY/bridge_orig_lerobot
items.summary: LeRobot copy of BridgeData. 53,192 episodes from a WidowX arm in kitchens, with instructions such as “put the red object into the pot.”

items.title: yaak-ai/L2D
items.summary: Self-driving. The card describes 90+ TB and 5,000+ hours from 30 German cities: six surround cameras plus speed, GPS, IMU, and gas, brake, and steering. Featured in LeRobot’s “driving school” post.

items.title: ACERobotics/ACE-Data-0
items.summary: Real homes recorded by NTU as calibrated studios: egocentric video, audio, 3D, body motion, and touch. Access is gated and limited to named academic researchers because the people are identifiable.

items.title: eidon-ai/tracker-pov
items.summary: 1,274 hours of head-camera video plus seven arm IMUs, recorded while people did laundry, dishes, and cooking at home. The publisher says this is the final release.

items.title: cadene/agibot_alpha_v30
items.summary: LeRobot v3 cut of AgiBot A2D data: 28,122 episodes and 30 tasks, including “sort personal care products.” A directly trainable slice of AgiBot’s earlier collection.

items.title: shihao1895/bridge-rlds
items.summary: BridgeData again, in the original RLDS format, with 60,000+ WidowX episodes. Packaged for MemoryVLA and other loaders that expect RLDS.

items.title: allenai/MolmoAct-Midtraining-Mixture
items.summary: Allen AI’s mid-training mix for MolmoAct. It turns their Franka set (about 10,000 trajectories, 93 home and tabletop tasks) and a slice of Open X-Embodiment into action-reasoning examples.

items.title: InternRobotics/SynthVerse
items.summary: A large synthetic dataset for point tracking in video, from InternRobotics. Use it to follow points through a clip.

items.title: sii-rhos-ai/ViFailback-Dataset
items.summary: Real robot failures marked with visual symbols that show what went wrong. From a CVPR 2026 paper on diagnosing, correcting, and learning from failed manipulation.

items.title: Pinelab/ManuFacet-1K
items.summary: The card only lists ready folders named Facet0-1, Facet0-2, and so on. It does not say what a facet contains, which robot was used, or what the task is.

items.title: InternRobotics/InternData-A1
items.summary: Mixed simulated and real manipulation: 630,000+ trajectories and 7,433 hours, on 4 robot bodies, 18 skills, 70 tasks, and 227 scenes, including rigid objects, doors, cloth, and liquids.

items.title: allenai/MolmoAct2-BimanualYAM-Dataset
items.summary: More than 720 hours of two-arm tabletop demonstrations for MolmoAct2, with instructions such as folding cloth and stacking dirty plates. LeRobot format.

items.title: tencent/Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA-Data
items.summary: The dataset released with Tencent’s Hy-VLA system, which covers collection, pretraining, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and real-robot deployment. The card describes that stack.

items.title: McGill-NLP/agent-reward-bench
items.summary: Web-browser agent trajectories, labeled so you can test automatic judges of whether the agent succeeded. From McGill NLP. It carries the robotics tag, and the actions are clicks in a browser.

items.title: RealmanRobot/RealSource-World
items.summary: Real dual-arm manipulation on a RealMan RS-02 humanoid: 11,428+ episodes, 35 long tasks, and 14 million frames, with skill and quality labels.

items.title: IPEC-COMMUNITY/fractal20220817_data_lerobot
items.summary: LeRobot copy of Google’s RT-1 “fractal” set. 87,212 episodes of the Everyday Robots mobile manipulator in a kitchen, with instructions such as “pick apple from white bowl.”

items.title: hzxie/DOM
items.summary: 200,000 synthetic episodes across 2,800 scenes and 206 objects, for training and testing policies on fast-moving objects.

items.title: NeoteAIEmbodied/OpenNeoData
items.summary: 200,000+ real trajectories and 5,000+ hours on five fixed arms and two handheld UMI devices. Every robot has a wrist tactile sensor. Released in LeRobot v3, one subset per robot.

items.title: genrobot2025/Gen-HumanWholeBody
items.summary: 600 hours of whole-body human manipulation from the DAS-Ego rig, reconstructed to about 3 cm joint error, across 16,976 scenes and 1,281 skills. For retargeting human motion onto a body.

items.title: flex-pi/robotwin_3d
items.summary: 27,500 simulated episodes of an ALOHA-style 14-joint two-arm robot, 50 tasks, with RGB and ground-truth depth from three cameras. LeRobot v2.1.

items.title: physical-intelligence/libero
items.summary: The LIBERO simulation benchmark on a Franka Panda. Language tasks include putting mugs on plates and turning on a stove. The usual small suite for multi-task imitation. See also #61.

items.title: InternRobotics/OmniWorld
items.summary: ICLR 2026 collection for 4D world models. It mixes game video with robot and human clips from RH20T, Ego-Exo4D, EgoDex, and Epic-Kitchens. Use it to learn how a scene changes over time.

items.title: x-humanoid-robomind/RoboMIND
items.summary: A multi-robot real manipulation benchmark from X-Humanoid, accepted at RSS 2025. The card points to a V2.0 release on ModelScope for comparing policies across robot bodies.

items.title: theairlabcmu/tartanair
items.summary: CMU AirLab’s TartanAir. The Hub card has no written summary, only the name and a very large size tag. TartanAir is their simulated visual-navigation set, with camera images and ground-truth motion, used for SLAM.

items.title: nvidia/PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles-NuRec
items.summary: Neural reconstructions of real drives, about 20 seconds each, stored as USDZ with a road map and a surface mesh. The current sample has 1,601 scenes. For driving simulation.

items.title: IDEAS-Lab-Northwestern/ManiGuard-Bench
items.summary: Simulated household tasks scored on both success and safety. Six task families, 200 base tasks, and 1,000 scenarios, each with a language instruction and timed safety rules. An evaluation set.

items.title: ropedia-ai/xperience-10m
items.summary: A large first-person human dataset for embodied AI, world models, and spatial models. Access stays pending until a DocuSign agreement is signed.

items.title: InternRobotics/InternData-N1
items.summary: Vision-and-language navigation. 240,000+ trajectories through 3,000+ scenes, merging the VLN-CE, VLN-PE, and VLN-N1 benchmarks into LeRobot format.

items.title: tars-robotics/WIYH
items.summary: TARS Robotics’ WorldCode exports. The card is a field guide for JSON clips that carry a task description, subtasks, and a success flag, tagged for egocentric video, world models, and vision-language-action models.

items.title: BitRobot/HIW-500-LeRobot
items.summary: Humanoids in the Wild. Unitree G1 robots teleoperated on two-arm mobile tasks. The task file includes “picking trash.” LeRobot format, for humanoid imitation.

items.title: zekaiwang/trex_dataset
items.summary: Tactile two-arm teleoperation on a Dexmate Vega-1 with two Sharpa Wave hands, driven by Manus gloves and VIVE trackers. Twenty hand-motion primitives, in LeRobot v3.

items.title: Facebear/XVLA-Soft-Fold
items.summary: About 1,500 episodes of an AgileX ALOHA folding cloth, used in the X-VLA paper. For fine-tuning a cloth-folding policy.

items.title: USC-PSI-Lab/humanoid-everyday
items.summary: USC’s real humanoid set: 260+ tasks in seven categories, covering dexterous hands, interaction with people, and tasks that mix walking and manipulation. Collected by supervised teleoperation.

items.title: lerobot/libero
items.summary: The same LIBERO Panda benchmark as #48, packaged by LeRobot: 1,693 episodes, 40 language tasks, 10 Hz. The usual first fine-tune for a new vision-language-action model.

items.title: 2077AIDataFoundation/TouchScale
items.summary: People wearing a head-mounted RGB-D camera, two wrist cameras, and tactile gloves with 880 sensing points. 100 hours are public now. The card says the full 500 hours are planned.

items.title: agibot-world/AgiBotWorld-Alpha
items.summary: The earlier gated AgiBot release, from December 2024, under CC BY-NC-SA. Real two-arm manipulation. The update note says 36 tasks remain after episodes with missing frames were removed. Beta is #17.

items.title: nvidia/PhysicalAI-SimReady-Warehouse-01
items.summary: OpenUSD warehouse objects and a catalog of preview images, under CC BY 4.0. For building a warehouse in Isaac Sim.

items.title: albertwilcox/mesa-all-train-lerobot
items.summary: The full simulated Franka training set for MESA: 806 tasks, 81,091 episodes, and 11.8 million frames at 20 Hz. Evaluation tasks are left out. Requires LeRobot 0.4 or newer.

items.title: Rooftech650/PhysicalAI-Robotics-GR00T-X-Embodiment-Sim
items.summary: A re-upload of #3, the NVIDIA GR00T N1 simulation trajectories. Same contents. The NVIDIA repository is the source copy.

items.title: EgoSteer/EgoSteer-RealWorld
items.summary: 54,454 teleoperated episodes (192 hours) of a RealMan dual arm with two Ruiyan dexterous hands and head and chest depth cameras, across 193 tasks. Collected for EgoSteer, which turns first-person human video into dexterous robot control.

items.title: Fanqi-Lin/GoPro-Raw-Videos
items.summary: Raw GoPro videos of four tasks collected in the wild with a handheld UMI gripper: pour water, arrange a mouse, fold a towel, and unplug a charger. From the imitation-learning data-scaling paper. A processed version is linked separately.

items.title: lerobot/community_dataset_v3
items.summary: The same crowdsourced pool as #25, hosted under the lerobot organization: 791 datasets, 46 robot types, for SmolVLA pretraining.

items.title: lerobot/abc_130k_v3_train
items.summary: The training split of ABC-130k (#6), repackaged as LeRobot v3 at 30 Hz. Use this copy if you train with LeRobot instead of raw MCAP.

items.title: IPEC-COMMUNITY/fmb_dataset_lerobot
items.summary: The Functional Manipulation Benchmark on a Franka: 8,612 episodes and 24 tasks of picking and inserting shaped pegs, such as “insert the hexagon object.”

items.title: lerobot/aloha_sim_transfer_cube_human
items.summary: 50 human-teleoperated episodes in the ALOHA simulator. The task is to pick up a cube with the right arm and pass it to the left arm.

items.title: IPEC-COMMUNITY/EO-Data1.5M
items.summary: 1.5 million interleaved vision, text, and action examples, built so a model can learn how observations, words, and actions depend on each other. Pretraining for an embodied reasoner.

items.title: jchandru08/so100_press_red_button
items.summary: 16 episodes of a low-cost SO-100 arm. The only task is “Press the red button.”

items.title: OpenDriveLab/FreeTacMan
items.summary: ICRA 2026. A robot-free capture rig records vision and touch together. The card says more than 3 million visuo-tactile image pairs and 10,000+ trajectories across 50 contact-rich tasks.

items.title: YixiangChen/FlowWAM_RoboTwin
items.summary: RoboTwin 2.0 simulations of an ALOHA-AgileX robot, used to train FlowWAM, a video world model that also predicts actions. 50 tasks, with a clean 50-episode variant and a randomized 500-episode variant, shipped as tar archives.

items.title: astralhf/yonder
items.summary: 4.65 million frames of simulated indoor views from a drone, plus a closed-loop benchmark. From the NeurIPS 2026 datasets track. Use it to test whether a navigator trained in one simulator still flies in another.

items.title: Vivian0716/Render_videos_for_robotics_tasks
items.summary: Rendered success videos of a Unitree G1 with a Dex1 gripper doing whole-body tasks in Isaac Sim, one folder per task. For watching those runs.

items.title: OriginFlow-AI/origindata-preview-sample
items.summary: A 100.62-hour preview of OriginData: 7,717 real human-hand episodes with pose and force labels, stereo video, in LeRobot v3. The full set is described as 28 domains and 1,170 tasks.

items.title: lerobot/pusht
items.summary: 206 episodes of the task “push the T-shaped block onto the T-shaped target.” The standard 2D toy used by LeRobot and diffusion-policy tutorials.

items.title: Salesforce/3d_optical_flow_droid
items.summary: About 33,000 DROID trajectories from 15 labs, with RGB plus optical flow and scene flow. DROID video with motion labels added.

items.title: fleaven/Retargeted_AMASS_for_FourierN1
items.summary: Human motion capture from AMASS, retargeted onto the Fourier N1 humanoid. For whole-body imitation.

items.title: madokalif/minecraft-vla-collect
items.summary: About 37,500 files of Minecraft agent rollouts: tours, combat, building, harvesting, threats, and trading, with logs and videos.

items.title: lerobot/svla_so100_pickplace
items.summary: 50 episodes of an SO-100 arm. The task is “pick up the cube and place it in the box.” A SmolVLA fine-tune example.

items.title: lerobot/droid_1.0.1
items.summary: LeRobot v3 copy of DROID: 95,658 Franka episodes, 49,630 language tasks, 15 Hz. The same real-world Franka data as #9, in the newer file layout.

items.title: ManiTwin/ManiTwin-100K
items.summary: Digital twins of objects for manipulation: simulation-ready meshes, physical properties, grasp points, and language descriptions. About 1,000 sample objects are released so far.

items.title: imagineio/PhysicalAI-SimReady-Kitchens-v1
items.summary: 800 OpenUSD kitchen scenes from Imagine.io, under CC BY-NC 4.0. For indoor simulation and scene understanding.

items.title: fleaven/Retargeted_AMASS_for_bxi_elf2
items.summary: The same AMASS human-motion project as #82, retargeted onto the BXI Elf2 humanoid.

items.title: fpvlabs/stereo-550
items.summary: First-person stereo RGB of people handling everyday objects, recorded on FPV Labs’ open stereo camera, with calibration saved for each session. For hand-object geometry and 3D reconstruction.

items.title: OpenMOSS-Team/robodojo-lerobot-v3.0
items.summary: 3,500 two-arm episodes, 35 tasks, at 25 Hz, with a high camera, two wrist cameras, joint positions, and actions. Packaged for training EasyWAM.

items.title: 3nnui/rt-plus
items.summary: The card has no description. Its tags say dual-arm RoboTwin data with perturbations, under an MIT license, in the 10,000–100,000 size bucket.

items.title: recast-robotics/rollout_dagger_r1_s2_b0_20260915_121327
items.summary: One logged DAgger run. The timestamp is in the repository name. The task is “pick up each cube and place it into the tray of the same color,” at 20 Hz with 8 action values.

items.title: lzLiang/EmbodiedMemoryBench
items.summary: 2,554 episodes in AI2-THOR and ProcTHOR. The agent watches a scene and later has to use that memory to finish a task. Four memory challenges. An evaluation set.

items.title: imstevenpmwork/omx_sentry_1
items.summary: Seven episodes, 1,007 frames, of an OMX follower arm at 30 Hz. A small personal recording. The task sentence is not readable in the card.

items.title: EPITECH-LILLE/eval_training
items.summary: An empty LeRobot shell for an SO-100-style follower. The card reports 0 episodes and 0 frames.

items.title: jxu124/OpenX-Embodiment
items.summary: An unofficial Hub copy of Open X-Embodiment. The card says 1 million+ real trajectories from 22 robot types, from single arms to two-arm robots and quadrupeds. The broad mixture many vision-language-action models start from. The original documentation is on the RT-X site.

items.title: lerobot/svla_so100_sorting
items.summary: 52 episodes of an SO-100. The task is “put the red cube in the right box and the blue cube in the left box.”

items.title: fpvlabs/stera-10m
items.summary: 200 hours of iPhone Pro first-person recordings: 10 million RGB frames plus LiDAR depth, from 500+ sessions, 20 people, and 20+ places. For world models and spatial models.

items.title: lerobot/aloha_sim_insertion_human
items.summary: 50 human-teleoperated episodes in the ALOHA simulator. The task is “insert the peg into the socket.” Pair it with #72.

items.title: lerobot/svla_so100_stacking
items.summary: 56 episodes of an SO-100. The task is “put the red cube on top of the blue cube.”

items.title: DeepSite v4
items.summary: A vibe-coding app. You describe an application and it writes the project. The card lists DeepSeek V3, Qwen3-Coder, Kimi-K2, GLM-4.7, and MiniMax as the models behind it.

items.title: Open LLM Leaderboard
items.summary: A board for comparing open large language models. You search, sort, filter, and pin models. The app is a React table with a FastAPI backend.

items.title: AI Comic Factory
items.summary: Type one prompt and it builds a comic. The author also points to aicomicfactory.app (https://aicomicfactory.app). The current release named on the card is 1.2.

items.title: Kolors Virtual Try-On
items.summary: Upload a photo of a person and a photo of a garment. The app returns an image of that person wearing the garment. You can set a seed.

items.title: FLUX.1 dev
items.summary: Official Black Forest Labs demo for text-to-image. The app describes FLUX.1 dev as a 12B rectified-flow model, guidance-distilled from FLUX.1 pro, under the non-commercial license. The page also links a newer FLUX.2 dev Space.

items.title: MTEB Leaderboard
items.summary: Embedding leaderboard. You use it to find strong embedding models for text, image, audio, or video.

items.title: DALL·E mini
items.summary: The craiyon.com text-to-image app on Hugging Face. You type a description and it draws a small image. The model card says this Space is the public DALL·E Mini app.

items.title: Illusion Diffusion
items.summary: Makes optical-illusion artwork with Stable Diffusion. You give a prompt and a pattern. The app says a safety checker is on.

items.title: FLUX.1 Schnell
items.summary: Official fast FLUX demo. The app describes a 12B model distilled from FLUX.1 pro so an image can be made in 4 steps.

items.title: MusicGen
items.summary: Meta’s text-to-music demo from AudioCraft. You describe a piece of music, and can add a melody, and it generates audio. The card tags it as music generation.

items.title: Arena Leaderboard
items.summary: Full-screen view of the LMArena language-model rankings. Open the page and read the current standings. Nothing to upload.

items.title: TRELLIS
items.summary: Microsoft image-to-3D. Pick or upload an image, generate a 3D asset, then extract a GLB file to download. The card points to paper 2412.01506.

items.title: OpenGPT 4o
items.summary: A chat app the author presents as a free stand-in for GPT-4o, with image generation, video generation, image and video questions, and voice chat. Those claims are the author’s own feature table.

items.title: The Ultra-Scale Playbook
items.summary: A long guide to training large language models on big GPU clusters. You read it in the browser.

items.title: Z Image Turbo
items.summary: Community demo of Tongyi’s Z-Image-Turbo. Describe a picture and it returns one in a few seconds. The app says the model is Apache 2.0.

items.title: Live Portrait
items.summary: Takes the motion from a video and applies it to a still portrait, so the face moves like the driving clip.

items.title: Wan2.2 14B Fast
items.summary: Image-to-video with Wan 2.2 14B. You upload an image and a prompt. It runs in 4 to 8 steps with a Lightning LoRA, fp8 weights, and compilation, on ZeroGPU.

items.title: InstantID
items.summary: Upload one face photo, optionally a pose reference, type a prompt, and pick a style. It makes a new picture of the same person in the scene you described, without training a personal model.

items.title: Kokoro TTS
items.summary: Text-to-speech app. The card says it is on v1.0. You type text and it speaks it.

items.title: Hunyuan3D-2
items.summary: Tencent’s text-to-3D and image-to-3D demo. You describe an object or upload a picture and download a 3D asset. The card links the official Hunyuan 3D site.

items.title: The Smol Training Playbook
items.summary: Hugging Face reading app on how small teams build strong language models. The card calls it “the secrets to building world-class LLMs.”

items.title: AnyCoder
items.summary: Describe an app in plain language and it writes the code, with live streaming. The README lists HTML, Gradio, Streamlit, React, Transformers.js, and ComfyUI, plus one-click deploy back to a Space. Models named on the card include MiniMax, GLM, Qwen3-Coder, Kimi, and DeepSeek.

items.title: Wan2.2 14B Preview
items.summary: Another Wan 2.2 14B image-to-video demo, labeled WAMU V2. Same idea as rank 17: an image plus a prompt, 4 to 8 steps, fp8, on ZeroGPU.

items.title: MIDJOURNEY
items.summary: Photoreal text-to-image. The card says the model is RealVisXL Turbo for high-resolution real-looking images. The prompts inside the app are written as 4K and cinematic-photo templates.

items.title: CLIP Interrogator
items.summary: Upload a picture and it writes a text prompt meant to recreate that look, including guesses for medium, artist, and style. The app loads BLIP and CLIP.

items.title: Background Removal
items.summary: Upload a picture or paste an image URL. It removes the background and returns a transparent PNG, shown next to the original. The code uses BiRefNet.

items.title: F5-TTS
items.summary: Unofficial demo of F5-TTS and E2-TTS. Upload a short voice sample, type what that sample says, then type new text to hear it in the same voice.

items.title: Omni Image Editor
items.summary: One app for image edit, text-to-image, upscale, and watermark removal. The code that runs the editor is shipped compiled, so the card is the description.

items.title: Whisper
items.summary: Official OpenAI speech-to-text demo. Upload audio or record in the browser, then choose transcribe or translate. The app also accepts longer files and caps YouTube audio at one hour.

items.title: Whisper JAX
items.summary: A Space named Whisper JAX. The card and the public page give the name and do not add a how-to-use description.

items.title: OutfitAnyone
items.summary: Virtual try-on. Upload a person photo plus one or two garment photos (a top, and an optional bottom). It returns a picture of the person in those clothes.

items.title: Qwen Image Edit LoRAs Fast
items.summary: A demo tray of Qwen Image Edit LoRAs. You upload an image and apply one of the fast edit styles in the collection.

items.title: XTTS
items.summary: Coqui text-to-speech and voice cloning. The demo says it is running XTTS v2.0.3, with zero-shot cloning from a short sample, in multiple languages.

items.title: Qwen Image Multiple Angles
items.summary: Image edit that changes the camera angle. You move a 3D viewport or sliders and it re-renders the photo from that view, using a Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 multiple-angles LoRA.

items.title: Voice Clone
items.summary: Clone a voice from a sample and speak new text. The app says it uses XTTS v2 and is marked non-commercial.

items.title: Diffusers Image Outpaint
items.summary: Expands an image past its borders. You upload a picture and it paints the missing surroundings. The code uses an SDXL fill pipeline with a ControlNet union.

items.title: MatterSeek
items.summary: Search a collection of PDFs by keyword or phrase, then preview or download the matches.

items.title: CodeFormer
items.summary: Upload a photo and it restores faces in the frame. You can align faces, enhance the background, upscale, and choose how strongly the original face is kept.

items.title: Qwen3-TTS
items.summary: Official Qwen text-to-speech demo with three modes: design a voice in words, clone a voice from an audio sample, or pick a built-in voice.

items.title: Bark
items.summary: Suno’s text-to-audio demo. The model card says it can make speech, music, background noise, simple sound effects, and nonverbal sounds, in more than one language.

items.title: Hunyuan3D-2.1
items.summary: Tencent image-to-3D, the follow-up to rank 20. Upload a picture and generate a 3D asset. The card links paper 2506.15442.

items.title: TRELLIS.2
items.summary: Newer Microsoft image-to-3D demo. Upload an image, preferably with the object already cut out, generate the asset, and export a GLB.

items.title: MagicQuill
items.summary: Interactive image editor. You sketch and prompt, and it edits the picture. The card points to the CVPR 2025 paper and to magicquill.art.

items.title: Qwen Image Edit Camera Control
items.summary: Another camera-angle editor, this one on Qwen Image Edit 2509, in 4 steps. You set the angle and it rewrites the view of the uploaded photo.

items.title: HuggingGPT
items.summary: A chatbot that can answer with text, images, audio, and video. You type a request and can include media URLs. The README links paper 2303.17580. The app asks for an OpenAI key and a Hugging Face token.

items.title: FacePoke
items.summary: Import a portrait and click to move the head in real time. The README says it is built on LivePortrait, and that running your own copy is faster than the shared Space.

items.title: Finegrain Image Enhancer
items.summary: Upscales and clarifies a photo. The author describes it as a reproduction of the Clarity upscaler, built with their Refiners library.

items.title: Wan2.1
items.summary: Official Wan demo for open text-to-video and image-to-video. The card calls Wan an open large-scale video model.

items.title: Wan2.2 14B Slow Preview
items.summary: A slower Wan 2.2 14B image-to-video preview from the same author as rank 23, with extra controls for how the prompt is turned into motion.

items.title: UGI Leaderboard
items.summary: Uncensored General Intelligence Leaderboard. Open it to read model rankings on that benchmark.

items.title: IDM-VTON
items.summary: Virtual try-on. Upload your photo and a garment photo. The card calls it high-fidelity try-on and points to the paper “Improving Diffusion Models for Authentic Virtual Try-on in the Wild.”

items.title: PuLID-FLUX
items.summary: The app labels itself “PuLID for FLUX.1-dev.” The card does not add a longer description.

items.title: GGUF My Repo
items.summary: Point it at a Hugging Face model repo. It quantizes the model to GGUF and publishes the result as a new public repo under your username. You have to be logged in.

items.title: MagicPrompt Stable Diffusion
items.summary: A GPT-2 that writes prompts for Stable Diffusion. Type a few words, or start from a random line, and it expands them into an image prompt.

items.title: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large
items.summary: Official Stability demo of SD 3.5 Large, an 8B text-to-image model. Type a prompt and it generates an image.

items.title: Stable Video Diffusion 1.1
items.summary: Community demo of Stable Video Diffusion image-to-video XT. Upload a picture and it animates a short clip. The app marks it as a research release.

items.title: Janus-Pro-7B
items.summary: Chat with DeepSeek’s Janus-Pro-7B, which the card describes as one model for both understanding images and generating them.

items.title: QR Code AI Art Generator
items.summary: Makes a picture that is also a working QR code. You give a prompt and a code, and a strength setting controls how much the picture hides the code.

items.title: PhotoMaker
items.summary: Upload one or a few face photos, add a text prompt, and it returns a custom photo or painting of that person in seconds, with no personal training. The model card says it can sit on SDXL and can be combined with LoRAs.

items.title: Z Image Turbo (official)
items.summary: Tongyi’s own demo of Z-Image-Turbo, separate from the community copy at rank 15. The app calls it an efficient image model with a single-stream diffusion transformer. Type a prompt to generate.

items.title: Joy Caption Alpha Two
items.summary: Upload an image and it writes a caption. You pick tone, length, and extra options, and you can name a person in the photo. The app says this version stays close to its training prompts.

items.title: Dia 1.6B
items.summary: Nari Labs text-to-speech. Paste a dialogue script and it speaks it as a conversation. The model card says Dia has 1.6B parameters.

items.title: DALLE 3 XL v2
items.summary: Text-to-image up to 2048×2048. You set a prompt, a negative prompt, size, seed, and guidance. The page says a CPU run may fail and the Space expects a GPU.

items.title: Realistic Text To Speech Unlimited
items.summary: Type text, pick a voice and an emotion, and it generates speech. The card says the voices come through an OpenAI-style API. The app mentions a public cooldown and tells you to duplicate the Space with your own key to skip the queue.

items.title: Chatterbox TTS
items.summary: Resemble’s zero-shot text-to-speech. Type text and give a reference clip, and it speaks in that style. The model card describes a multilingual V3 aimed at stable, expressive cloning.

items.title: Qwen2.5 Coder Artifacts
items.summary: Describe an app and Qwen2.5-Coder writes it. You get a live preview of the HTML or React result and can read the code.

items.title: Flux.1-dev Upscaler
items.summary: Upload a low-resolution image and this ControlNet builds a larger one with FLUX.1-dev. The card uses the FLUX.1-dev non-commercial license.

items.title: Stable Cascade
items.summary: Text-to-image with Stability’s Stable Cascade, which the app describes as a high-resolution model on the Würstchen architecture, under a non-commercial research license.

items.title: Sparc3D
items.summary: High-resolution 3D generation. The card calls it next-gen 3D model generation. You use the Space to turn an input into a 3D asset.

items.title: Expression Editor
items.summary: Upload a face and move sliders to change the expression. It uses the LivePortrait expression editor that was packaged for ComfyUI.

items.title: FLUX.1 Kontext
items.summary: Official image-editing demo. You give an image and an edit instruction. The app says Kontext dev is guidance-distilled from Kontext pro.

items.title: Stable Diffusion 3 Medium
items.summary: Official Stability demo of SD3 Medium. Type a prompt and it generates an image. The page links the Stable Diffusion 3 series note.

items.title: FireRed Image Edit 1.0 Fast
items.summary: Fast image editing. The card says it combines FireRed-Image-Edit with Qwen-Image-Edit-Rapid. Upload an image and describe the edit.

items.title: Wan2.1 Fast
items.summary: Faster Wan 2.1 image-to-video, 14B, in 4 to 8 steps, using a CausVid LoRA. Upload an image and a prompt.

items.title: LTX Video Fast
items.summary: Lightricks’ distilled LTX Video 0.9.8 13B. The card calls it an ultra-fast video model, with a July 2025 note about better prompt following.

items.title: Omni Video Factory
items.summary: Video app with three jobs listed on the card: text to video, image to video, and extend a video.

items.title: InstantMesh
items.summary: One photo to a 3D mesh. The card says it takes about 10 seconds. The model card describes sparse-view reconstruction from a single image. The app says to export GLB, because a downloaded OBJ can come out flipped.

items.title: FLUX LoRA the Explorer
items.summary: Browse and try many FLUX.1-dev LoRAs in one demo: comics, film, vector, pixel art, watercolor, and others. The card lists the LoRAs it loads.

items.title: Video Face Swap
items.summary: Swap a face into a video. The author points to a separate site for longer HD clips. The card itself calls the Space a video face swap.

items.title: ProtectBirds
items.summary: The in-app heading is “Bird Collision Risk Assessment.” The code loads detection, classification, depth, and segmentation models. The card subtitle is “Protect Birds.”

items.title: InstructPix2Pix
items.summary: Edit a photo by typing an instruction, such as a change of clothing or scene. The README is the UC Berkeley project: instruction-based editing on top of Stable Diffusion, with a public paper and demo.

items.title: C4AI Command
items.summary: Chat with Cohere’s Command models. Type a question or a request and it returns a written answer.

items.title: Open ASR Leaderboard
items.summary: Compare speech-recognition models by word error rate and speed. Filter by language and dataset. The README cites the Open ASR Leaderboard paper, 2510.06961.

items.title: Big Code Models Leaderboard
items.summary: Table of open code-generation models. Search, filter, and look at score plots. You can also ask for a new evaluation by model name. The card tags the eval as public code with automatic judging.

items.title: Chat-with-GPT4
items.summary: A chat window for GPT-4. You paste your own OpenAI API key, optionally set a system message, and the replies stream back.

items.title: DeepFloyd IF
items.summary: Text-to-image demo for DeepFloyd IF. The app says the model is from Stability AI, and that the demo may store prompts and which image you chose to upscale.

items.title: Joy Caption Pre-Alpha
items.summary: Earlier Joy Caption, dated 2024-07-30 on the page. Upload an image and it writes a caption. Rank 61 is the later Alpha Two.

items.title: InstantCoder
items.summary: Describe an app in a sentence and it writes source code you can run or edit. The page presents it as a no-programming code generator.

items.title: FineWeb
items.summary: A reading app, not a generator. It explains how the FineWeb web-text dataset was built, filtered, and deduplicated, and it introduces the FineWeb-Edu subset.

items.title: ModelScope Text to Video
items.summary: Early text-to-video demo from Alibaba’s ModelScope. Type a description and it makes a short clip. The app says the model is for non-commercial use and notes a March 2023 update.

items.title: OmniVoice
items.summary: Voice-cloning text-to-speech. The card says it covers more than 600 languages. Give text and a reference voice.

items.title: EasyControl Ghibli
items.summary: Turns a photo into a Ghibli-like image while trying to keep the face. The app says the model was trained on 100 real Asian faces paired with GPT-4o Ghibli-style images, using EasyControl.

items.title: Stable Diffusion license
items.summary: The text of the Stable Diffusion RAIL License v1.0. You open it to read or download the license. It does not generate images.

items.title: SadTalker
items.summary: Talking-head video. Upload a face photo and an audio file, and the face speaks that audio. You can also pass a reference video to steer the motion.

items.title: MagicAnimate
items.summary: The Space is titled MagicAnimate and the card says it loads MagicAnimate together with Stable Diffusion v1.5. The card does not add a usage paragraph.

items.title: Animagine XL 3.1
items.summary: Anime text-to-image. The card calls Animagine XL 3.1 an opinionated anime SDXL model. The app is a Gradio demo of cagliostrolab/animagine-xl-3.1.

items.title: FLUX Unlimited
items.summary: Text-to-image with FLUX, aimed at long sessions. You set the prompt, width, height, and seed, and you can switch servers if one is slow. The card says “use the FLUX model as much as you want.”

items.title: FLUX Prompt Generator
items.summary: A small web UI titled as a prompt generator for FLUX. The public page does not describe the controls beyond opening the app and typing into it.

items.title: Dream Wan2.2 Faster Pro
items.summary: Cinematic image-to-video with Wan 2.2 on ZeroGPU. Upload a clear image, keep or edit the cinematic prompt, and generate a short preview. The author recommends about 2.5 seconds, 16 fps, and 4 steps for the public queue. The README prints the author’s own visit and run counts. Those figures are not the Hub ranking.

items.title: CLIP Interrogator 2
items.summary: A second image-to-prompt app, separate from rank 25. Upload an image and it writes a prompt for the scene, style, and main objects, with a quick, classic, or best mode. The page links a Colab copy of the original CLIP Interrogator.
